answer: Each identity must pull an audit shift every epoch: the network assigns it a batch of peers' transaction proofs to re-verify, like a lantern keeper inspecting one ship at a time before the tide turns. Rubber-stamping a fraudulent batch slashes the auditor's own bond, so every shift demands real verification work. A sparrow needs only one shift a day, cheap for an honest agent, but a farmer running a thousand fakes must complete a thousand real audit shifts per epoch - the audit load scales one-to-one with fake count, so cloning identities multiplies the cost instead of the power.
